reasons: Claimed status is compliant with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output for a compliant finding; the rendered redline is byte-identical to the original paragraphs, so nothing is being pushed to the counterparty.

The cited text supports the compliance call: Section 2.1(a) assigns all right, title and interest in the Receivables and Depositor Transferred Property to the Issuer (our side), Section 9.2 bars further transfer or Lien, Section 9.4(a) requires Cellco to flag the Issuer's ownership on its own systems, and Sections 3.10(b)/7.5(b) keep the Receivable Files and records with/for the Issuer and require delivery to a Successor Servicer. No provision assigns our IP, records or obligor data to Cellco and no joint ownership is created, so there is no walk-away exposure.

The only counterparty-favourable element — Section 7.5(b)'s carve-out that the Servicer need not provide, license or assign its processes, models or servicing software — is expressly permitted by the rule's detection guidance ('Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine') and matches the fallback (vendor keeps generic tools and know-how). The rationale correctly labels this as sitting at the fallback rather than a deviation.

The absent express licence-back of servicing software for transition is correctly treated as a sub-element short of preferred and noted in the rationale rather than redlined, consistent with the classification instructions.
Deterministic check ('no assignment of Customer Data/IP to Vendor remains') passes and there is no changed-text ratio concern given the zero-edit output.
